hook.question_in_my_head: Why would the navy send a ship to sea when it nearly rolled over in a test? And is 'she' a ship? What happens to it?
hook.why: The contradiction promises a disaster, but 'thirty sailors ran across' is odd and unexplained, and 'brand-new warship' with no name or setting gives little to grip.

who.thirty_sailors: Run across the deck for the stability test.
who.the_navy: Sends the ship anyway, to please the king.
who.the_admiral: Stops the test and wishes the king were there; unclear why.
who.the_king: Away at war, wants the mightiest warship, keeps sending letters to get her to sea; ordered the cannons.
who.builders_and_officials: Afraid to tell the king; a builder says 'Only God knows' at the hearing.

what_happened: Thirty sailors run across a new warship's deck and she almost capsizes in the test.
The admiral stops the test and says he wishes the king were there.
The king, away at a war, wants the most powerful ship and demands she be sent to sea.
The Vasa is given two decks of heavy bronze cannons stacked high above the water.
Nobody dares tell the king, and his letters keep demanding she sail.
On launch day a crowd watches the sails go up.
A light gust tips her over, she recovers, and the crowd keeps waving.
A second gust tips her further and the open lower gun ports dip below the waterline.
Water floods in and she sinks in the harbour in front of the city.
At the hearing the builder says only God knows why, and nobody is punished because the king was the one who ordered the cannons.
She was top-heavy: heavy weight high, too little ballast low.
Adding more stone would have lowered the gun ports into the water, so there was no easy fix.
The dock test had already shown how she would sink.
why: A ship stays upright when its weight is low, like sand in the bottom of a bottle. The Vasa had heavy bronze cannons stacked high and not enough stone ballast low, so she was top-heavy and a gust could tip her. Adding more ballast would have made her ride lower, putting the lower gun ports near the water, so there was no easy fix. And nobody would tell the king.
twist: The failed dock test with the sailors was a literal preview of how the ship would sink: the warning was ignored and the disaster was foretold.
